question:
In the given figure BD is perpendicular to AC then what will be the measure of angle AEB?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/807d8cd1ca51ff649567f3b95eea75f645aef18b854df740ad20fc6d0e50e138.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles are **complementary** (their sum is 90°).

From the property of the **altitude** BD ⊥ AC, triangle ADE is a right-angled triangle at D.

Given the internal angle ∠DAE = 10° from the figure geometry.

⇒ ∠AED = 90° − 10° = 80°.

Since the point B lies on the line segment ED (or ray ED), the angle ∠AEB is equal to ∠AED.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** BD ⊥ AC, which implies ∠ADB = 90°. Point E lies on the altitude BD. From the provided geometry, ∠DAE = 10°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41b7859aa35a2d549a10f2a013e9c34d5d6d28d875a65ac59d7c34673d029f3c.png] 

In **▵ADE**, the sum of all internal angles must be 180°.

⇒ ∠DAE + ∠ADE + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ 10° + 90° + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ 100° + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ ∠AED = 180° − 100°

⇒ ∠AED = 80°

Since points **B, E, and D** are collinear on the same perpendicular line, ∠AEB is the same as ∠AED (assuming B is positioned such that E is the vertex of the angle formed with ray EB).

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Complementary Angles in Right Triangle

In a right-angled triangle, if one angle is 90°, the other two acute angles must sum to 90°.

Orthocenter Property

The altitude of a triangle is the perpendicular segment from a vertex to the opposite side. The intersection of altitudes is the orthocenter.</p
